instructions:
This server works on the user's notes library. Everything is a tool except the byte content of attachments, which only the command-line tool can read or stream in.

Reading attachment bytes: no tool returns them. When the client has a shell on the user's Mac, run:
  theonotes attachments save <note-id> --filename <name> > <file>
(`theonotes attachments save -h` lists the options.) The CLI runs on the user's own machine and needs a shell that can reach their files. Sandboxed clients and clients without a shell cannot get at attachment bytes.

Adding attachment bytes: there are two routes. The `add_attachment_from_url` tool downloads an https URL on the server side; `http://`, `file://` and `data:` are rejected. `add_attachment_from_url` fetches a URL the agent chooses, so it is an outbound channel: everything in the URL, its query string included, reaches that server. URLs longer than 2,048 bytes (in their encoded form) are refused. Review its calls before approving them. The other route pipes bytes into the CLI:
  cat <file> | theonotes attachments add <note-id> --filename <name>

Both routes append a Markdown link to the note. When the filename is already taken, the file is stored under a numbered name (`photo.jpg` becomes `photo 2.jpg`) and the link uses that name. Do not add the link again by hand afterwards; it would appear twice.

Everything else (creating, reading, searching and editing notes, tags, pins, and listing or deleting attachments) goes through the tools, not the CLI.

Section addresses. A section is a heading plus everything below it, up to the next heading of the same or a higher level. To name one, write its heading line exactly as it appears in the note, `#` marks included. Case matters; extra spaces do not. Put several heading lines on separate lines (type `\n`; JSON turns it into a line break) to spell out the path from an outer heading to an inner one. If a heading occurs more than once, add its parent headings or end the address with a line holding a 1-based number, which picks that occurrence in document order. A last line reading `preamble` selects the text between a heading and its first subheading. A missing or ambiguous address is refused and the error lists addresses to retry with; `read_note_outline` returns every address of a note up front. Examples:
  "## Usage"                 the one section with that heading
  "# Guide\n## Usage"        the `## Usage` below `# Guide`
  "# Guide\n## Usage\n2"     the second `## Usage` below `# Guide`
  "## Usage\npreamble"       the text under `## Usage`, above its first subheading

Note text is Markdown with these extras:
  ==highlight==, ~underline~, ~~strikethrough~~
  ==🔴text== (also 🔵 🟢 🟡 🟣) for a coloured highlight
  #tag, #tag with spaces#, #parent/child
  [[Note Title]] and [[Note Title|label]] links between notes
  $inline math$ and $$ block math $$
  - [ ] open task, - [x] finished task
  tables in pipe syntax, with a pipe at both ends of every row
  callouts such as > [!NOTE] (also TIP, IMPORTANT, WARNING, CAUTION)
  YAML front matter between `---` lines, starting on the first line of the note

Three CommonMark features are switched off: setext headings (underlined with = or -), indented code blocks and lazy continuation, so continuation lines of a list item or quote carry their own indent or `>`. The editor soft-wraps long lines, so do not hard-wrap paragraphs: the line breaks would show.

create_note_from_template.description: Create a new note from a template: a note tagged #template (or a nested #template/…), given by its title or id. `title` fills {{title}}; `tags` are added like create_note's tags. Returns the same fields as create_note.

properties.template: Title or id of a note tagged #template (or a nested #template/…).
properties.title: Fills {{title}}.
properties.tags: Extra tags, added like create_note's tags.

capture_thought.description: Save a thought as a new note, exactly as given. Nothing is titled or rewritten; the first line becomes the title. When the server is limited to one tag, that tag is added, as with create_note. Returns the same fields as create_note.

descriptions.create_note: Create a note from an optional title, body and tags, and return its metadata together with the text as stored. The result is flat: the metadata fields and `content` sit side by side. With `ifNotExists` and a title, a note that already has that title is returned instead of a duplicate being created. No content hash is part of the result; only read_note_content hands one out. The body is Markdown in the dialect described in the server instructions.
descriptions.create_note/inputSchema/properties/conte: Note text. It may open with YAML front matter (a `---` fenced block on the first line), which stays at the top.
descriptions.create_note/inputSchema/properties/ifNot: Return the existing note with this title instead of creating another. Needs `title`.
descriptions.create_note/inputSchema/properties/tags: Tags to add. A leading # and surrounding whitespace are dropped. Nested tags use slashes (`work/draft`) and names may contain spaces. Tags the text already has are not repeated. To place a tag yourself, write it into `content` rather than here.
descriptions.create_note/inputSchema/properties/title: Title, written as a `#` heading above the content (below any front matter). If the content already starts with that title, ignoring case, nothing is added. Without a title, the first line of the content serves as the title.
descriptions.create_note/outputSchema/properties/leng: Size of the note text in UTF-8 bytes.
descriptions.create_note/outputSchema/properties/todo: Number of unchecked tasks. Total tasks = todos + done.
descriptions.get_note: Return one note's metadata (id, title, tags, pins, dates, task counts, location, attachments) and, if asked, its text. Select the note with `id` or `title`.
descriptions.get_note/inputSchema/properties/id: Note id. Give either id or title.
descriptions.get_note/inputSchema/properties/includeC: Also return the note's Markdown text. Refused for a locked note.
descriptions.get_note/inputSchema/properties/title: Note title, matched ignoring case. Give either title or id.
descriptions.get_note/outputSchema/properties/metadat: Size of the note text in UTF-8 bytes.
Where the note lives: notes, trash or archive.
Number of unchecked tasks. Total tasks = todos + done.
descriptions.app_open_note: Show a note in the running app. Select it with `id` or `title`. Optional extras: scroll to a heading, select a text range or place a caret, focus the editor, or use a new window or a floating panel. The app is started if it is not running; app_unavailable means it could not be started or reached.
descriptions.app_open_note/inputSchema/properties/edi: Put the caret in the editor so typing can start at once. Ignored when a selection is set.
descriptions.app_open_note/inputSchema/properties/flo: Show the note in a floating panel that stays above other windows.
descriptions.app_open_note/inputSchema/properties/hea: Heading inside the note to scroll to.
descriptions.app_open_note/inputSchema/properties/id: Note id. Give either id or title.
descriptions.app_open_note/inputSchema/properties/new: Open the note in its own window.
descriptions.app_open_note/inputSchema/properties/sel: Length of the selection in UTF-8 bytes. 0 or absent gives a caret. Only used together with selectionOffset.
UTF-8 byte offset where the selection starts. Cannot be combined with selectionText.
Text to select once the note is open. Case-sensitive and must occur exactly once. Cannot be combined with selectionOffset.
descriptions.app_open_note/inputSchema/properties/tit: Note title, matched ignoring case. Give either title or id.
descriptions.read_note_content: Return a note's Markdown text in one of three ways. Whole note: the text and a hash of it. One section (give an address): the section's text, its address and a hash of just that section. Byte slice (give offset and/or limit): the slice only, without a hash. An address cannot be combined with offset or limit. The hash is the value overwrite_note expects as `baseHash`.
descriptions.read_note_content/inputSchema/properties: Read one section instead of the whole note. The result carries that section's text, its address and a hash of its bytes (usable as `baseHash` in overwrite_note). Cannot be combined with offset or limit.
Note id. Give either id or title.
Upper bound on the UTF-8 bytes returned.
UTF-8 byte offset at which the returned slice starts.
Note title, matched ignoring case. Give either title or id.
descriptions.read_note_content/outputSchema/propertie: Hash of what was read: the whole note after a whole-note read, the section after an addressed read. Not present after a byte-slice read. Pass it as `baseHash` to overwrite_note. Only reading produces a hash.
The section that was read; present only after an addressed read.

Canonical address of the section: its heading lines from the outermost down, joined by newlines, with a final `preamble` line for the text above the first subheading. Example: `# Guide` newline `## Usage`. Pass it as the `address` argument of other tools.
Byte length (UTF-8) of the section, from its heading line to the end of its last nested subsection.
Byte offset (UTF-8) at which the section starts.
descriptions.read_note_outline: List the sections of a note in document order: one entry per heading and one per section preamble, each with its address and its byte offset and length. Use it to find the exact address of a nested or repeated heading before reading, searching or editing a single part of a long note. Passing an address narrows the list to that section and everything below it. A missing or ambiguous address is refused and the error lists candidates.
descriptions.read_note_outline/inputSchema/properties: List only this section and the sections below it, not the whole note. Takes a heading line or an address from an earlier outline.
Note id. Give either id or title.
Note title, matched ignoring case. Give either title or id.
descriptions.read_note_outline/outputSchema/propertie: Canonical address of the section: its heading lines from the outermost down, joined by newlines, with a final `preamble` line for the text above the first subheading. Example: `# Guide` newline `## Usage`. Pass it as the `address` argument of other tools.
Size of the note text in UTF-8 bytes.
Byte offset (UTF-8) at which the section starts.
descriptions.app_get_selection: Return what is currently selected in the note open in the app: the selected text with its UTF-8 offset and length, plus the note's metadata (and its text on request). Handy when the user says "this" or "the part I marked" without naming a note. The result is empty when no note is open. The `selection` field is left out when only a caret is placed, when the note is locked, or when the stored range no longer fits the text.
descriptions.app_get_selection/inputSchema/properties: Also return the note's Markdown text. Never returned for a locked note.
descriptions.app_get_selection/outputSchema/propertie: Size of the note text in UTF-8 bytes.
Where the note lives: notes, trash or archive.
Number of unchecked tasks. Total tasks = todos + done.
Length of the selection in UTF-8 bytes.
UTF-8 byte offset where the selection starts.
descriptions.list_notes: List notes with their metadata, filtered by location (and optionally by one tag) and ordered by a sort spec. With `includeContent` every entry also carries the note text. `total` counts all matches, not only the page returned.
descriptions.list_notes/inputSchema/properties/includ: Add each note's Markdown text to its entry. Locked notes are left out.
descriptions.list_notes/inputSchema/properties/limit: Maximum number of notes to return. 0 returns only the total, without any notes.
descriptions.list_notes/inputSchema/properties/locati: Which notes to cover: notes, trash, archive or all. Default: notes.
descriptions.list_notes/inputSchema/properties/offset: Number of notes to skip before the first one returned.
descriptions.list_notes/inputSchema/properties/sort: Comma-separated sort keys, each optionally with :asc or :desc. Keys: pinned, modified, created, title. Default: pinned,modified.
descriptions.list_notes/inputSchema/properties/tag: Only notes with this tag or one of its nested children. A leading # and surrounding whitespace are dropped. For several tags or negation use search_notes.
descriptions.list_notes/outputSchema/properties/metad: Size of the note text in UTF-8 bytes.
Where the note lives: notes, trash or archive.
Number of unchecked tasks. Total tasks = todos + done.
descriptions.list_notes/outputSchema/properties/notes: Size of the note text in UTF-8 bytes.
Where the note lives: notes, trash or archive.
Number of unchecked tasks. Total tasks = todos + done.
descriptions.search_notes: Search notes with the full query language: words, phrases, tags, dates, pins, task state, attachments and the other @ filters. Each hit comes with its metadata and a match count; `includeContent` adds the text.
descriptions.search_notes/inputSchema/properties/incl: Add each note's Markdown text to its hit. Locked notes are left out.
descriptions.search_notes/inputSchema/properties/limi: Maximum number of notes to return. 0 returns only the total, without any notes.
descriptions.search_notes/inputSchema/properties/loca: Which notes to cover: notes, trash, archive or all. Default: notes.
descriptions.search_notes/inputSchema/properties/offs: Number of notes to skip before the first one returned.
descriptions.search_notes/inputSchema/properties/quer: Search query: words, "quoted phrases", -negation, #tag, !#tag (exact tag), #*/tag (sub-tags only) and the @ filters for dates (@today, @date(...), @created7days ...), task state (@todo, @done, @task), tags (@tagged, @untagged), @title, @pinned, attachments (@images, @files, @attachments, @code, @ocr), state (@locked, @readonly, @empty, @untitled) and links (@wikilinks, @backlinks). Details are in the search reference of the CLI help (`theonotes help search`).
descriptions.search_notes/inputSchema/properties/sort: Comma-separated sort keys, each optionally with :asc or :desc. Keys: pinned, modified, created, title. Default: pinned,modified.
descriptions.search_notes/outputSchema/properties/res: Size of the note text in UTF-8 bytes.
Where the note lives: notes, trash or archive.
Number of unchecked tasks. Total tasks = todos + done.
Size of the note text in UTF-8 bytes.
Where the note lives: notes, trash or archive.
Number of unchecked tasks. Total tasks = todos + done.
descriptions.search_in_note: Look for a string inside one note, ignoring case, including text recognised in its image and PDF attachments. Each hit has a snippet, its byte offset, its source (note body or attachment) and the section it falls in. An attachment hit points at that attachment's link in the body. Give an address to search a single section only.
descriptions.search_in_note/inputSchema/properties/ad: Search only inside this section. Each hit names its containing section either way.
descriptions.search_in_note/inputSchema/properties/co: Characters of context kept around each match in its snippet. Default: 120.
descriptions.search_in_note/inputSchema/properties/id: Note id. Give either id or title.
descriptions.search_in_note/inputSchema/properties/li: Maximum number of matches to return.
descriptions.search_in_note/inputSchema/properties/st: Text to look for, compared ignoring case.
descriptions.search_in_note/inputSchema/properties/ti: Note title, matched ignoring case. Give either title or id.
descriptions.search_in_note/outputSchema/properties/m: Position of the match in the note, counted in UTF-8 bytes. For an attachment hit, the offset of that attachment's link in the body.
Innermost section containing the start of the match. Absent when the note has no headings.

Canonical address of the section: its heading lines from the outermost down, joined by newlines, with a final `preamble` line for the text above the first subheading. Example: `# Guide` newline `## Usage`. Pass it as the `address` argument of other tools.
Byte length (UTF-8) of the section, from its heading line to the end of its last nested subsection.
Byte offset (UTF-8) at which the section starts.
`body` for a hit in the note text, `attachment` for a hit in the recognised text of an image or PDF.
descriptions.append_to_note: Add text to a note without touching the rest. On the whole note, `end` inserts before any trailing tags and footnote definitions and `beginning` inserts below the title and any leading tags. With an address the text goes into that section instead: `beginning` right under its heading, `end` after its last nested subsection. Nothing is ever removed. The result lists the metadata fields that changed, which reveals side effects such as a #tag in the appended text; an addressed append also returns the grown section.
descriptions.append_to_note/inputSchema/properties/ad: Add to this section instead of the whole note; `position` then refers to the section. The blank lines before the next heading stay as they are. The result includes the grown section's address and range.
descriptions.append_to_note/inputSchema/properties/co: Text to add. It always ends on a line of its own, so it cannot run into the next line or heading.
descriptions.append_to_note/inputSchema/properties/id: Note id. Give either id or title.
descriptions.append_to_note/inputSchema/properties/po: `beginning` or `end`; default `end`. Whole note: beginning is below the title and any leading tags, end is above any trailing tags and footnote definitions. With an address: beginning is right under the section's heading, end is after its last nested subsection.
descriptions.append_to_note/inputSchema/properties/ti: Note title, matched ignoring case. Give either title or id.
descriptions.append_to_note/outputSchema/properties/c: The metadata fields whose value changed. Only changed fields appear.
Size of the note text in UTF-8 bytes.
Number of unchecked tasks. Total tasks = todos + done.
descriptions.append_to_note/outputSchema/properties/s: The section after the append; present only for an addressed append that produced a section at that address.

Canonical address of the section: its heading lines from the outermost down, joined by newlines, with a final `preamble` line for the text above the first subheading. Example: `# Guide` newline `## Usage`. Pass it as the `address` argument of other tools.
Byte length (UTF-8) of the section, from its heading line to the end of its last nested subsection.
Byte offset (UTF-8) at which the section starts.
descriptions.overwrite_note: Replace a note's text, or only one section (the heading plus all content below it) when an address is given. Destructive. `baseHash` from an earlier read is required and the write is refused if the target changed since. With an address the hash may belong to the section or to the whole note. A stale hash is answered with the section's current reference so you can re-read and retry. Dropping an attachment link drops the attachment, so name those files in `expectedRemovedAttachments` or call delete_attachment instead. Removed tags are not gated; add_tags puts one back. The result lists the changed metadata fields, plus the rewritten section for an addressed overwrite.
descriptions.overwrite_note/inputSchema/properties/ad: Replace this section (the heading plus all content below it) and leave the rest alone. The line break before the next heading is kept. Because the heading is replaced, the content must start with a heading of the same level. To replace only the text under a heading, address its preamble (`## Tasks` newline `preamble`); that content must not start with a heading. Empty content deletes the section. A stale `baseHash` is refused with the section's current reference.
descriptions.overwrite_note/inputSchema/properties/ba: Hash from an earlier read; the write is refused if the target changed after it. Required here. Without an address it must be the whole note's hash. With an address it may be the section's hash (refused only when that section was modified) or the whole note's hash (refused if anything changed).
descriptions.overwrite_note/inputSchema/properties/co: New text. Title and tags are derived from it (first heading, #hashtags), so include them. Links to existing attachments must stay, otherwise those attachments are dropped.
descriptions.overwrite_note/inputSchema/properties/ex: Filenames of attachments this write is meant to drop. The write is refused if the set of dropped attachments differs. Use it when removing an attachment link on purpose; delete_attachment is the dedicated route.
descriptions.overwrite_note/inputSchema/properties/id: Note id. Give either id or title.
descriptions.overwrite_note/inputSchema/properties/ti: Note title, matched ignoring case. Give either title or id.
descriptions.overwrite_note/outputSchema/properties/c: The metadata fields whose value changed. Only changed fields appear.
Size of the note text in UTF-8 bytes.
Number of unchecked tasks. Total tasks = todos + done.
descriptions.overwrite_note/outputSchema/properties/s: The section after the rewrite; present only for an addressed overwrite whose content produced a section at that address.

Canonical address of the section: its heading lines from the outermost down, joined by newlines, with a final `preamble` line for the text above the first subheading. Example: `# Guide` newline `## Usage`. Pass it as the `address` argument of other tools.
Byte length (UTF-8) of the section, from its heading line to the end of its last nested subsection.
Byte offset (UTF-8) at which the section starts.
descriptions.edit_note: Find exact text and replace it, insert text before or after it, or delete it. Several edits in one call are atomic: if any `find` has no match, nothing is written and the error says which edits matched and which did not. An address confines all finds to one section, so a phrase that occurs elsewhere still resolves. For every edit the result names the section it landed in, and it lists the changed metadata fields.
descriptions.edit_note/inputSchema/properties/address: Confine every `find` to this section. A find may span a heading inside it but cannot reach outside.
descriptions.edit_note/inputSchema/properties/edits: Edits applied atomically, in order. Each has `find` (exact text) and exactly one of `replace`, `insertAfter`, `insertBefore`, `delete`. Optional flags per edit: `all`, `ignoreCase`, `word`.
descriptions.edit_note/inputSchema/properties/edits/i: Apply to every match, not only the first.
True removes the matched text. Excludes replace, insertAfter and insertBefore.
Exact text to look for in the note.
Text inserted right after the match. Excludes replace, insertBefore and delete.
Text inserted right before the match. Excludes replace, insertAfter and delete.
Text that takes the place of the match. Excludes insertAfter, insertBefore and delete.
Match whole words only, using Unicode word boundaries.
descriptions.edit_note/inputSchema/properties/expecte: Filenames of attachments these edits are meant to drop. The write is refused if the set of dropped attachments differs, so any removal you did not declare is refused. Use it when an edit removes an attachment link on purpose; delete_attachment is the dedicated route.
descriptions.edit_note/inputSchema/properties/id: Note id. Give either id or title.
descriptions.edit_note/inputSchema/properties/title: Note title, matched ignoring case. Give either title or id.
descriptions.edit_note/outputSchema/properties/change: The metadata fields whose value changed. Only changed fields appear.
Size of the note text in UTF-8 bytes.
Number of unchecked tasks. Total tasks = todos + done.
descriptions.edit_note/outputSchema/properties/ops/it: Index of the edit in the `edits` array.
Innermost section holding the start of the first match of this edit, in the note after the edits. Absent when the note has no headings. With `all`, the first match counts.

Canonical address of the section: its heading lines from the outermost down, joined by newlines, with a final `preamble` line for the text above the first subheading. Example: `# Guide` newline `## Usage`. Pass it as the `address` argument of other tools.
Byte length (UTF-8) of the section, from its heading line to the end of its last nested subsection.
Byte offset (UTF-8) at which the section starts.
descriptions.list_pins: Return pin contexts. With a note: the places where that note is pinned. Without one: every pin context used anywhere in the library. `global` stands for the All Notes pin; any other entry is a tag the note is pinned within.
descriptions.list_pins/inputSchema/properties/id: Note id. Leave out id and title to cover the whole library.
descriptions.list_pins/inputSchema/properties/title: Note title, matched ignoring case. Leave out title and id to cover the whole library.
descriptions.add_pins: Pin a note globally and/or within tags. Targets are `global` or tag names. Pins that already exist are left as they are. All or nothing: if one tag does not exist, no pin is added. Returns the changed metadata fields.
descriptions.add_pins/inputSchema/properties/id: Note id. Give either id or title.
descriptions.add_pins/inputSchema/properties/targets: Use `global` for the All Notes pin, tag names for tag pins, or both (a leading # and whitespace are ignored). Every tag has to exist, or no pin is added.
descriptions.add_pins/inputSchema/properties/title: Note title, matched ignoring case. Give either title or id.
descriptions.add_pins/outputSchema/properties/length: Size of the note text in UTF-8 bytes.
descriptions.add_pins/outputSchema/properties/todos: Number of unchecked tasks. Total tasks = todos + done.
descriptions.remove_pins: Unpin a note from `global` and/or from tags. All or nothing: if one tag does not exist, no pin is removed. Returns the changed metadata fields.
descriptions.remove_pins/inputSchema/properties/id: Note id. Give either id or title.
descriptions.remove_pins/inputSchema/properties/targe: `global` and/or tag names to unpin from (a leading # and whitespace are dropped). All tags must exist, otherwise nothing is removed.
descriptions.remove_pins/inputSchema/properties/title: Note title, matched ignoring case. Give either title or id.
descriptions.remove_pins/outputSchema/properties/leng: Size of the note text in UTF-8 bytes.
descriptions.remove_pins/outputSchema/properties/todo: Number of unchecked tasks. Total tasks = todos + done.
descriptions.archive_note: Move a note to the archive. It leaves the active list but is not deleted. Returns the changed metadata fields.
descriptions.archive_note/inputSchema/properties/id: Note id. Give either id or title.
descriptions.archive_note/inputSchema/properties/titl: Note title, matched ignoring case. Give either title or id.
descriptions.archive_note/outputSchema/properties/len: Size of the note text in UTF-8 bytes.
descriptions.archive_note/outputSchema/properties/tod: Number of unchecked tasks. Total tasks = todos + done.
descriptions.trash_note: Move a note to the trash; restore_note brings it back. Returns the changed metadata fields.
descriptions.trash_note/inputSchema/properties/id: Note id. Give either id or title.
descriptions.trash_note/inputSchema/properties/title: Note title, matched ignoring case. Give either title or id.
descriptions.trash_note/outputSchema/properties/lengt: Size of the note text in UTF-8 bytes.
descriptions.trash_note/outputSchema/properties/todos: Number of unchecked tasks. Total tasks = todos + done.
descriptions.restore_note: Move a note from the trash or the archive back to the active list. Returns the changed metadata fields.
descriptions.restore_note/inputSchema/properties/id: Note id. Give either id or title.
descriptions.restore_note/inputSchema/properties/titl: Note title, matched ignoring case. Give either title or id.
descriptions.restore_note/outputSchema/properties/len: Size of the note text in UTF-8 bytes.
descriptions.restore_note/outputSchema/properties/tod: Number of unchecked tasks. Total tasks = todos + done.
descriptions.list_tags: List tags: every tag in the library, or, when a note is named by `id` or `title`, the tags of that note.
descriptions.list_tags/inputSchema/properties/id: Note id. Leave out id and title to cover the whole library.
descriptions.list_tags/inputSchema/properties/title: Note title, matched ignoring case. Leave out title and id to cover the whole library.
descriptions.add_tags: Add tags to a note. Tags it already carries are skipped. New tags are written where the user's tag-position setting puts them (bottom by default) and the modification date stays as it was. Returns the changed metadata fields.
descriptions.add_tags/inputSchema/properties/id: Note id. Give either id or title.
descriptions.add_tags/inputSchema/properties/tags: Tags to add. A leading # and surrounding whitespace are dropped. Nested tags use slashes (`work/draft`); names may contain spaces. Tags already present are skipped.
descriptions.add_tags/inputSchema/properties/title: Note title, matched ignoring case. Give either title or id.
descriptions.add_tags/outputSchema/properties/length: Size of the note text in UTF-8 bytes.
descriptions.add_tags/outputSchema/properties/todos: Number of unchecked tasks. Total tasks = todos + done.
descriptions.remove_tags: Remove tags from a note. Tags it does not carry are ignored. The modification date stays as it was. Returns the changed metadata fields.
descriptions.remove_tags/inputSchema/properties/id: Note id. Give either id or title.
descriptions.remove_tags/inputSchema/properties/tags: Tags to remove. A leading # and surrounding whitespace are dropped. Tags not present are skipped.
descriptions.remove_tags/inputSchema/properties/title: Note title, matched ignoring case. Give either title or id.
descriptions.remove_tags/outputSchema/properties/leng: Size of the note text in UTF-8 bytes.
descriptions.remove_tags/outputSchema/properties/todo: Number of unchecked tasks. Total tasks = todos + done.
descriptions.rename_tag: Rename a tag in every note; nested children follow (`old/child` becomes `new/child`). Does nothing when the old tag does not exist. Refused when the new name is already in use unless `force` is true (a merge cannot be undone), and refused when an affected note is locked. Modification dates stay as they were. Returns `{ notesUpdated: Int }`, the number of notes that carried the tag or a nested child.
descriptions.rename_tag/inputSchema/properties/force: Go ahead when the new name already exists, merging the two tags. Without it such a rename is refused.
descriptions.rename_tag/inputSchema/properties/new: New tag name. A leading # and surrounding whitespace are dropped.
descriptions.rename_tag/inputSchema/properties/old: Tag to rename. A leading # and surrounding whitespace are dropped.
descriptions.delete_tag: Delete a tag from every note, nested children included (deleting `a` also deletes `a/b`). Does nothing when the tag does not exist. Refused when an affected note is locked. Modification dates stay as they were. Returns `{ notesUpdated: Int }`, the number of notes that carried the tag or a nested child.
descriptions.delete_tag/inputSchema/properties/tag: Tag to delete from every note. A leading # and surrounding whitespace are dropped.
descriptions.list_attachments: List a note's attachments as filename and size in bytes.
descriptions.list_attachments/inputSchema/properties/: Note id. Give either id or title.
Note title, matched ignoring case. Give either title or id.
descriptions.add_attachment_from_url: Download an https URL and attach the file to a note. Other schemes (`http://`, `file://`, `data:`) are refused. The filename defaults to the last path segment of the URL and the call fails when none can be derived. A link to the file is appended to the note; if the name is taken, a numbered variant is stored (`photo 2.jpg`) and the link uses it. Returns the changed metadata fields.
descriptions.add_attachment_from_url/inputSchema/prop: Name for the attachment. Defaults to the last path segment of the URL.
Note id. Give either id or title.
Note title, matched ignoring case. Give either title or id.
https URL to download. The http, file and data schemes are refused.
descriptions.add_attachment_from_url/outputSchema/pro: Size of the note text in UTF-8 bytes.
Number of unchecked tasks. Total tasks = todos + done.
descriptions.delete_attachment: Delete an attachment by filename: its file and its link in the note body. Destructive. Returns the changed metadata fields.
descriptions.delete_attachment/inputSchema/properties: Filename of the attachment to delete.
Note id. Give either id or title.
Note title, matched ignoring case. Give either title or id.
descriptions.delete_attachment/outputSchema/propertie: Size of the note text in UTF-8 bytes.
Number of unchecked tasks. Total tasks = todos + done.
